decision: production holds 1 human, 1 AI account, 311 tasks, 183 comments (181 by the AI), 7 projects, 3 sections, 1 label, 11 reads, 1540 log rows, 8 images, 199 shares (197 public task links, 1 project edit share, 1 whole-space AI share), 0 access rows, 0 push rows

decision: one global space (one Durable Object holding every user's rows plus the server-only tables) instead of one space per user
why: cross-user rules (guest admission, access recompute, push plan, purge) stay single transactions as they are in Postgres today, and the clients stay single-space with one cursor; per-user filtering moves into the server's pull
evidence: writes.ts needs advisory locks and savepoints only because Postgres runs batches concurrently; a DO transaction is single-threaded

decision: admit/landed/view hooks, space.write, client unauthorized+rejected+onStatus, worker headers
why: procrastimate's server rules need a per-request actor inside the sync transaction and guest-filtered pulls
evidence: hooks.test.ts 9 tests, client 11 tests, core 151, web 4 in chromium+webkit
result: pushed feat/app-hooks; first commit attempt failed the web hook once under parallel load, passed alone and on retry

decision: deleted write-cost and read-cost tests, and the two retried-delete tests
why: statement counts measured Postgres round trips through Hyperdrive; SQLite runs in the object's process, so a statement is microseconds; a write and its bookkeeping now commit in one transaction, so the crash-between state the retry tests built cannot exist

decision: production Postgres dumped read-only into the new backup format: 311 tasks, 183 comments, 1540 log rows, 199 shares, 8 images, 2 users, 4 sessions, 1 account
why: the restore loads the same format the daily R2 backup writes, so the import and disaster recovery are one path

decision: parity: the AI account's token reads /api/view, /api/links, and every task's /api/activity and /api/comments from old production and from a Bun server holding the import; 624 routes, 0 differ
why: the agent API reads every synced and server-only table the clients show, through the server's own rules
evidence: scripts/sync-engine-migration/parity.ts; links compared by id without the origin-bound url, order was undefined on both

decision: the web client runs on sync-engine/client-web; full e2e suite 74 passed across chromium and webkit
why: the specs are the feature map's checks

decision: e2e WebKit contexts are persistent and each names its own OPFS database file through a test-only localStorage key
why: Playwright's persistent WebKit contexts share one OPFS store across profiles: a second context opened the first one's database, client id and all; localStorage stays per context
evidence: probe3: localStorage null, OPFS lists the other context's file

decision: added beforePush so the web worker uploads image bytes before the writes that list them
why: the old upload sent images first; without it another device synced a task whose image 404ed for 30 s
evidence: images.e2e.ts offline image test failed, then passed

decision: parity against wrangler dev, with the App object restoring the production dump from local R2 on its first start: 624 routes, 0 differ

evidence: scripts/sync-engine-migration/parity.ts against :6320; old production answered bursts with 503 and the harness retries 5xx

decision: people search runs one select per source instead of a UNION ALL of seven
why: a Durable Object's SQLite refuses it: too many terms in compound SELECT; bun:sqlite allows it, so only Worker-mode e2e caught it
evidence: e2e list-header, sharing, ramble failed under E2E_WORKER=1 only, then passed

decision: restoreDump's empty-database guard is a typed select
why: the raw count read an array under bun:sqlite and never refused
evidence: backup.test.ts 'a restore refuses a database that already holds a user'

decision: iOS runs on the engine's Swift client over plain GRDB tables in a new sync.sqlite; verified on the simulator against a Bun server: sign-in pulled a server task, a quick-add task reached the server stamped client ios, and a server write appeared live
why: throwaway XCUITests through ./sim test; the server's log rows read api task put, ios settings patch, ios task put
